<!-- pr-reviewer: b2b596b663426a33da89d63c43dcbde047b22ff0 -->

**Verdict: ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings.** (P2, safety floor: read-only converter, no posted-G-code consumer yet — the pinning tests pass and the move rules are as documented.)

## What looks good
- The converter is read-only over the plan: it emits the steps of each level in the plan's order and refuses a step it cannot emit with a named reason. No re-planning, no drop, no added cut. The module doc lists the rules and the move invariants; the refusal constants are all present and named.
- Checked values: `EmitHeights::new` rejects non-finite or clearance-below-top (`BAD_HEIGHTS`); `EmitFeeds::new` rejects non-positive or non-finite (`BAD_FEEDS`).
- `Emitted` carries `cut_moves` (the exact move ranges of each cut), `entries`, `stays`, `lifts` and `exits`, so callers can audit what the plan covered.
- The exact-circle arc split (quarter turns ending on plan points) and the chord fallback for leads/helices/ramps are tested (`an_exact_circle_becomes_arcs`, `each_step_kind_gives_its_moves`, `nothing_is_dropped`).
- The k4 test helper keeps both sides of the merge conflict: the load stage sits between order and link in the plan builder, and the path goes through the real converter. `k3_load` reads `cuts_path_with`, which reproduces the old test pen from the same plan (same moves, same notes, per the temporary comparison).

## Results merged with side/path-kernel (df9ec30b6)
Built locally in a fresh worktree (`.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4279-review`, head `b2b596b6`, clean trial merge — `git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/side/path-kernel` reports "Already up to date", no conflicts). Local is the requested build for this sub-PR; no self-hosted runner was started.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib kernel_emit`: **7 passed** (7/7).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws`: **31 passed** (31/31, including `k4_order_link`, `k6a_plan_emit`, `k3_load`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: **pass** (no warnings).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: **7 steps, all ok, 0 failed** (`cargo xtask gate light`, release, on this head): light build 542s, motion light lib 350s, adaptive_troch_island 43s, adaptive_troch_neck 17s, adaptive_troch_parallel 11s, app pocket_pass_start 3s, app offset_pass_start 57s — wall 17.2 min.

No example catalog suite was needed: no post or toolpath generator is changed (the converter is uncalled by recipes — the only consumers are the new tests).

## The widening (ask a): no real gouge is hidden
The pin area moved from `fixture::band` (stock grown by 2 tool radii, less the part) to `st.offset(4.0 * R).unwrap().difference(&part)` (4 tool radii). What the 2-radii area did: the verifier (`Mode::Area`) read the synthetic band and the part loop, and reported **72 Gouge warnings on the disc Outside** and **84 on the dog bone Outside**. What the 4-radii area does: **0 Gouge warnings**, no `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock`, and each descent below the stock top is a plan entry (a ramp or a helix; Outside entries are air entries with an arc lead).

Every 2-radii warning is on an air entry or its arc lead, outside the band: measured as the moves whose WARN line pairs map to the lead feeds (e.g. disc moves 1619-1622, 1815-1819, 3664-3667, 3860-3864; dog bone moves 2-4, 34-38, 190-192, 257-261, 440), standing at y ≈ -28.9 to -30.4 (the stock edge is y = -25), i.e. 4.4 mm or more beyond the stock, and 17 mm or more from the part. The part loop is subtracted unchanged in both areas — the part-boundary check (the real law: every chord below the stock top stays `r - leave - tol` from every edge of the region) is identical in both areas. The widening only moves the synthetic outer boundary 2 tool radii (8 mm) outward, so it acquits exactly those air leads. The verifier's part check — the gouge of the part, the thing the safety floor protects — is unchanged. The interior check (the disk, the dog bone) is identical in both areas and reads 0 in both.

**Verdict: the widening is legitimate. It does not hide a real gouge.** No real gouge of the part was removed by the change; the removed 72/84 warnings were the verifier reading the synthetic outer boundary in the air, which the wider legal room of the entry stage legitimately covers.

## The move rules and refusal constants (ask b)
Verified by reading the code (`kernel_emit/mod.rs`, `pen.rs`, `arcs.rs`):
- **Lateral rapid only at/above the clearance height** — the builder is seeded at `clearance_z`; `air_move` pushes `Rapid` only if both ends are at/above `clearance_z - EMIT_TOL`. `entry`'s rapid is at `max(at_z, clearance_z)`.
- **Rapid along the tool axis goes only up** — `retract` pushes a `Rapid` only when the tool stands below the retract plane and then sets state Clear.
- **Plunge-feed down from the clearance height to the approach** — `air_move` pushes `Plunge` (plunge feed) whenever the move goes below the tool's current height.
- **Below the stock top, only moves of a proved step** — descent (`Plunge`), lead-out (`Feed`), cut (`Feed`), stay-down link (`Feed`), lead (`Feed`); `air_move` is refused above the stock top (`APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL`).
- **Each step starts where the tool stands** — `expect_down(start)` requires `Down` and `at ≈ start`, else `STEP_NOT_DOWN` / `STEP_OFF_TOOL`.
- **Arcs only for exact circles** — a cut whose curve holds an exact circle (`curve.arc()`) becomes G2/G3 arcs (quarter turns ending on plan points, `arcs.rs`); leads, helices, ramps and non-circle cuts are chords.
- **Plane must be the setup XY plane** — `Frame::of` refuses any other plane (`NOT_SETUP_XY`); the mapping reads the work plane's origin and depth.
- **Nothing dropped, nothing added** — `end <= begin` after an arc run refuses (`CUT_DROPPED`); `emit_levels` emits exactly the plan's steps, refusing `UNKNOWN_STEP`; `end_level` requires Clear (`ENDS_DOWN`).
- Refusal constants: `BAD_HEIGHTS`, `BAD_FEEDS`, `NOT_SETUP_XY`, `AXIS_NOT_NORMAL`, `UNKNOWN_STEP`, `ENTRY_NOT_CLEAR`, `APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL`, `STEP_OFF_TOOL`, `STEP_NOT_DOWN`, `ENDS_DOWN`, `ARC_OFF_CIRCLE`, `ARC_NOT_MONOTONE`, `CUT_DROPPED`, `NOT_FINITE` — all present and named.

The 7 unit tests exercise the rules (move-rule invariant, each step kind, lift notes, exact-circle arcs, level order, nothing dropped, refusal by name, empty plan). There is one corner the rules do not cover, noted below as a question (not blocking): `air_move`'s rapid branch can push a vertical rapid down if the plan carries an approach point above the clearance height while the tool stands higher along an exit retract; no kernel plan produces such an approach (the entry stage's approach is at `top + clearance`, below the clearance height), so it is not reachable from the kernel — noted, not requested.

## The k4 merge resolution (ask c)
The resolution keeps both sides:
- The load stage is between order and link in the plan builder: `let controlled = load.map(|(stage, lc, reader)| stage.control(ordered.clone(), &r, reader, &lc, R).unwrap());` — and the curves come from the controlled set (`controlled.as_ref().and_then(Verdict::out).map_or(ordered.curves(), |c| c.set().curves())`).
- The path goes through the real converter: `kernel_path_with` builds the plan (guide → order → load stage → link → entry/exit stage), then `convert(plan)` → `emit_plan(plan, plane, h, f).unwrap()`, and asserts `out.cut_moves.len() == cuts` and `out.lifts == tally.lifts()`.
- `cuts_path_with` (the new helper for `k3_load`) reproduces the old pen-style moves (rapid ×2 + plunge per entry, feed along cuts/stay-down links, rapid up at the end, one note per lift reason). It is the same plan, built the same way; the PR documents a temporary test comparing the two paths as having the same moves and notes.

## The k3_load re-pin (ask d)
The pin moved the disc Outside ConstantEngagement row from `[334, 118, 74]` to `[337, 118, 77]` (comment names the cause: #4265 was gated without #4253; #4253 changes that row). Verified on this head: the full `kernel_laws` suite passes, and the measured readings are `over 337 worst 118`, with 7 lifts named 7 — matching the pin. The unnamed over-move places are on the stock edge line (x ≈ ±34 to ±40, y ≈ -25), consistent with #4253's link edge band keeping the Outside starts at the stock edge. The other three rows are unchanged and also pass (disc Inside `[3507, 173, 0]` / `[833, 173, 1]`; dog bone Inside `[2587, 173, 0]` / `[581, 173, 1]`; dog bone Outside `[724, 167, 3]` / `[678, 143, 66]`). The pre-merge side-head numbers (334/74) are cited from the PR body and were not re-measured independently — the pin is self-consistent on this head and the assertion passes.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Questions / notes
1. The k4 pin keeps the Outside lift counts at 13 (disc) and 15 (dog bone). PR #4275 (the approach from the air) touches the same `k3_load.rs` Outside rows and makes the Outside lift counts of the K4 pin 0. Both are open; whichever merges second takes a merge of `side/path-kernel` and re-pins the rows. This is an ordering note, not a defect in this PR.
2. The 44 (disc) and 52 (dog bone) Outside feeds outside `fixture::centre_reach` are the same arc leads in the air — a reading of the entry stage, not of the converter (noted in the PR body; no pin asserts it).
3. `UNKNOWN_STEP` is unreachable from any kernel plan step — no test can make it, as documented. Fine.
4. The `air_move` corner in the rules section above is theoretical; the converter refuses `APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL` above the stock top but does not refuse an approach point above the clearance height when the tool stands higher along a retract. Out of scope for this PR (no kernel plan produces it), but worth a one-line note to the next person who edits `air_move`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Verdict: ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings.** (Delta re-review on `143a6ffaf` after the refresh of `side/path-kernel` that carries #4275. P2, side-branch sub-PR. Built locally - the runner refuses this PR by design, see below.)

## What this covers

The head moved from `b2b596b663` (the head of the last independent review) to `143a6ffaf` (the merge of `origin/side/path-kernel` fd653b0, which contains #4275, the air approach). The old review does not count for this head. This review is the delta review of the merge.

## Delta (b2b596b663..143a6ffaf)

Clean DELTA. The only hand edits are in test and doc files:

- `crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws/k3_load.rs`: the `READ` rows of #4275 are kept (disc Outside `[415, 145, 19]` / `[344, 122, 81]`, dog bone Outside `[739, 180, 13]` / `[683, 143, 69]`). The 337 / 77 row of this PR is replaced. The Inside rows are unchanged. The doc comment names the cause.
- `crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws/k4_order_link.rs`: the real converter is kept, the lift counts of #4275 (0 each) are kept, the `CROSSINGS` table replaces the zero pin (disc Outside 3, dog bone Outside 1, Inside 0), and `entries` / `stays` / `exits` are asserted against the plan.
- `docs/decisions/4269-kernel-plan-converter.md`: the new section "The merge of #4254".

No kernel or converter source changed. No new dependency, no process file, no snapshot PNG, no build.rs, no `.github/`, no `.cargo/`, no `xtask/`.

## The runner (read, not built)

The runner was dispatched for this head (run 45946156909, `pr-test.yml`). It failed at the step "Not a read-only PR": the workflow diffs the head against `origin/main`, not against the side-branch base. The sub-PR base drags in side-branch files (`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `crates/motion/Cargo.toml`, `crates/pathkernel/Cargo.toml`, `xtask/src/*.rs`), so the run refuses by design. The PR's own files vs `side/path-kernel` are read-only (9 files, motion source + tests + docs). The refusal is a workflow limitation for side-branch sub-PRs, not a verdict on this PR. Local verification instead, in my own worktree.

## Local verification (the trial worktree, trial merge against `origin/side/path-kernel`, clean, the merge result is identical to the head)

- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-motion`: pass
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib kernel_emit`: 7/7
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws k3_load`: 1/1 - the pinned rows hold on the merged tree (disc Outside over 415 / 344, worst 145 / 122, 19 / 81 unnamed; dog bone Outside over 739 / 683, worst 180 / 143, 13 / 69 unnamed; Inside unchanged)
- `k4_order_link`: 1/1 - lift counts 0 on each case; `CROSSINGS` measured: disc Outside 3 (moves 5, 189 / 1664 / 1882, at (-38.398, -28.993)), dog bone Outside 1 (move 4 / 33, at (4.587, -28.866)), both Inside 0; entries, stay-down links and exits assert against the plan
- `k6a_plan_emit`: 1/1 - no `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock`, no `Gouge`; only `Crossing` warnings (3 on disc Outside, 1 on dog bone Outside); 1 entry each, Inside read as a ramp (the helix is chords)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass

(`cargo build`-adjacent runs on this head, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6.)

## The ruling on the crossing feeds (the one open point)

**#4279 may merge with the counts 3 and 1 pinned. #4300 stays open as a P7 follow-up.**

- The crossings are feeds in the air, one tool radius outside the stock. No material is involved. The verifier pin finds no gouge, no rapid in stock or in the part and no plunge into stock.
- The pin is named and bounded: `CROSSINGS` asserts the counts exactly. Any new or missing crossing goes red. It is not a silent drop of a quality law.
- The converter is inert: no recipe or app caller exists yet (#3752 not landed). The crossings cannot reach a posted G-code from this PR.
- #4300 (P7) is a quality law - the link proof does not read the leads of the entry stage. It is tracked, and it is not a safety-floor issue. It is not a merge blocker for this PR.
- The caveat that matters: a recipe that turns a converted plan into a posted path (#3752) must not ship with the crossings as-is. It waits on #4300, or the converter refuses the path there. That is a work order on the follow-up, not a blocker for this PR.

One check owed by the first pass, answered: whether the four-radii verifier area hides a real gouge. No. The checked region is the stock grown by four tool radii, less the part. The part surface stays a region boundary, so a disc center within `r - leave - tol` of the part still raises `Gouge`. The growth only removes the spurious outer-boundary gouges of the air entries, whose arc leads reach up to 1.5 radii out (17 mm or more from the part).

## Notes (not blocking)

- The light lane was NOT run on this head. The body records: "not run on this head (7 steps, 0 failed on `b2b596b`)". I do not claim a light-lane pass. The light-lane result on `b2b596b` is a different head and does not count here.
- `k3_load` reads `cuts_path_with` (no entry leads), so its `crossings == 0` assertion is honest by construction. The `k4` pin is the one that reads the leads.
- The commits end with `Refs #4269`, not `Fixes #4269`. Partial work is defensible: the converter has no app caller yet. #4269 stays open until the recipe lands.
- New test file `k6a_plan_emit.rs` is a new file in an existing directory suite (`kernel_laws/`). It has no reason line in the body, which is not needed - that rule is for top-level binaries.
- Provenance line present; `docs/decisions/4269-kernel-plan-converter.md` records the re-pin rationale.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
